native.admission_inspect: A salt-pitted brass cup, no bigger than a thumb. Its film sits higher than the shadow.
apply_texts: A thin salt-line settles where no tide reaches. The measure is exact and unwelcome.
For a breath the cup is only worn brass. The false depth loosens, then remains.
Grit sorts into a depth too large for the cup, then stills. You cannot name the error.
Last warmth leaves the brass. The false tide-line holds, small, and will not explain.
The film breaks under the thumb. Cold grit shifts, as if a longer line paid out.
The line repeats, no wider. Repetition makes the small wrongness harder to set aside.
The palm reads a depth the room does not have. Brass gives back only salt and cold.
You tilt the cup. The film climbs the wrong wall and stops, obedient to nothing here.
You turn the cup. The grit keeps its false depth. Nothing else in the hand moves.
inspect_texts: A salt-pitted brass cup, no bigger than a thumb. Its film sits higher than the shadow.
A thumb-smear has lowered the film. The new line is wider than the cup.
Salt grit holds a false level. The cup stays small. The error does not.
The cup weighs like a wet line. Distance gathers in the palm and will not name itself.
The film has settled wrong. You cannot say if the fault is light or measure.
The film is torn. Grit in the hollow feels deeper than the brass is wide.
The same wrong tide-line, no wider than before. Smallness does not correct it.
Thumb-sized brass cup. The inner film sits a hair above the shadow it ought to cast.
native.name: Salted Sounding Cup
